game: NYG @ DET, kickoff 2025-11-23 13:00 ET, DET -14, total 50.5, roof dome, weather forecast not saved

script.base: Detroit leads by about two scores and finishes near the implied 32.2-18.2. Goff scores early through St. Brown (33 targets, 197 yards, 322 air in weeks 9-11) and Jameson Williams (20/273/207), then the lead back runs: Gibbs 36 carries/206 and Montgomery 32/138 against a NYG run defense allowing 5.85 YPC and 52 runs of 10+. NYG, with Jaxson Dart out, trails and throws; Tracy (38/177) and Singletary (32/107) lose carries. Dome, so no weather drag. A priced -14 is not by itself a fourth-quarter sit, but a bigger lead would cut DET starter snaps.
script.flip1: NYG stays within one score. Detroit cannot salt the clock, so Williams, St. Brown and LaPorta (13 targets, 150 yards) stay live and Gibbs's late carry bump shrinks while his 15 targets/140 receiving yards stay relevant. Winston does not have to abandon the run, so a Tracy rush under dies and NYG pass volume is smaller than the trail script.
script.flip2: Sewell (ankle), Decker (shoulder), Glasgow (knee) and Ratledge (knee) are limited or out, with Frazier already out, and the DET run and deep timing stall. Detroit leans short (St. Brown, LaPorta, Gibbs catches) or the game becomes a sub-50.5 slog. The other blowout version: DET is up big by halftime and Gibbs and Williams sit before the numbers clear.

pre_mortem: It's Monday and this lost because Detroit led big, Sewell and Decker were limited, and Montgomery took the second-half clock while Gibbs sat on about 40 rush yards and one catch, a replay of the 28 rush+rec game rather than the 218/172/146. Williams saw two shots, the second half was all runs, and he finished under 54.5 the way he did in the 0 game; NYG's secondary injuries never mattered because Detroit did not need to throw once the 5.85 YPC run defense collapsed. The same Monday would have buried a Johnson over if Winston never looked at the TE, which is why that Dart-era 138-yard role was not a leg. If that counter-case feels stronger than the first-half banking assumption, drop Williams and keep Gibbs only.
slip_story: One story only: Detroit controls a dome game near 32-18 and gets there through Gibbs's all-purpose role plus at least a first-half vertical shot to Williams before the clock kill. Same-direction DET offense stack, not a shootout and not a total under. Williams is the script-dependent leg; Gibbs is the anchor that also survives a closer game via the 15-target receiving path. Do not add Tracy rush over, a NYG pass over that needs a shootout, St. Brown, or a second market on either player. No TD legs. No price, so the slip is a logged read, not a bet.
